empty.title: No workspace yet
empty.body: A workspace is an AI team working in one app folder: the orchestrator splits your task into subtasks for its teams, follows the flow you draw, and the audit layer checks every result. Start with a new folder, or let an agent read an app you already have.
empty.folderWithout: This folder has no workspace yet.
empty.pick: Pick a workspace on the left, or add one.

permission.title: Agents will run without asking
permission.body: This workspace runs its sessions with bypassed permissions: agents edit files and run commands in its folder without asking you first.
permission.hint: You can switch to a stricter mode in the workspace settings. With stricter modes, approve tool calls by opening the session in chat.

settings.title: Workspace settings
settings.name: Workspace name
settings.maxParallel: Sessions running at the same time
settings.maxParallelHint: Subtask and audit sessions together, per task (1–6).

modeHints.bypassPermissions: Agents act without asking. Fastest, but review the result.
modeHints.acceptEdits: File edits are allowed; other tools wait for approval in chat.
modeHints.default: Every tool call waits for your approval in chat.

providers.title: Connect an AI provider
providers.subtitle: Agents run on the provider CLIs installed on the server this app runs on. Log in to at least one; only connected providers show up in the model list.
providers.hint: Connect opens a terminal on the server (your VPS, for example) and runs the provider's login command there. The login stays on that server; the workspace never stores an API key.
providers.noneBanner: No AI provider is connected yet, so agents cannot run
providers.disconnectedBanner: Agents use a provider that is not connected: {{providers}}

addWorkspace.title: Add workspace
addWorkspace.intro: A workspace always works in one folder. Where should this one work?
addWorkspace.newBody: Start an app from scratch in a new, empty folder, with the default teams.
addWorkspace.existingBody: Point at its folder; an agent reads the code and proposes teams that fit it.
addWorkspace.newFolderHint: Type the full path of the new folder (it is created for you), or browse to a parent folder and add the name.
addWorkspace.existingFolderHint: The folder of the app. Nothing in it is changed while it is analysed.
addWorkspace.alreadyHasWorkspace: This folder already has a workspace.
addWorkspace.setupIntro: How should the workspace for {{name}} be staffed?
addWorkspace.analyseTitle: Let an agent analyse the app
addWorkspace.analyseBody: It reads the repository (read-only) and proposes teams and roles for this app. You review them before anything is created.
addWorkspace.noProvider: Connect a provider first to run the analysis.
addWorkspace.useDefaults: Skip the analysis and use the default teams
addWorkspace.reviewIntro: Proposed teams. Rename, edit, remove or add before creating; the orchestrator and the audit layer are added for you.
addWorkspace.summary: About the app (given to the orchestrator)
addWorkspace.backgroundHint: You can close this dialog: the analysis keeps running on the server and shows up in the workspace sidebar, where you can reopen it to review the result.
addWorkspace.waitingForAgent: Waiting for the agent to start…
addWorkspace.githubTitle: From GitHub or another git server
addWorkspace.githubBody: Clone a repository (https with a token, or git@… over the server's SSH keys), then the teams are proposed from what it contains.
addWorkspace.cloneInto: Clone into this folder (the repository gets its own subfolder)
addWorkspace.tokenNew: Paste a token for this clone
addWorkspace.githubHint: Tokens are managed in Settings. An SSH URL uses the SSH keys of the server this app runs on. Agents push and pull with the same access.
addWorkspace.cloneNoPath: The clone finished but did not report where it went.
addWorkspace.kindIntro: What kind of work is this workspace for?
addWorkspace.workNewBody: Start from a new, empty folder. Upload your material later from the files tab.
addWorkspace.workExistingBody: A folder that already holds your documents, data or material. Original files are never changed or deleted.
addWorkspace.workExistingFolderHint: The folder with your documents or data. Agents work here and save results in a results/ subfolder.
addWorkspace.privacyNote: The server is yours, but file contents the agents read are still sent to the AI provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) while they work. Keep data that must not leave out of this folder, and check figures and documents before you use them.
addWorkspace.customIntro: Build your own team. For each member: the team name, the agent name, their job in one sentence, then the full role (what they do, the rules, the result format). The coordinator and QA are added automatically.
addWorkspace.customDescriptionPlaceholder: Their job in one sentence, e.g. "writes short video scripts"
addWorkspace.customRolePlaceholder: The full role: what they do, the rules to follow and the result file format.
addWorkspace.customChecksPlaceholder: e.g. every price must match the price list file; each script at most 60 seconds; no typos.

flow.explain: Work of {{to}} waits until the work of {{from}} in the same task is done. Teams on separate branches run in parallel.

work.teamPlaceholder: Prompt or list of work for this agent. Ctrl+Enter sends.
work.notePlaceholder: Note for this work (Ctrl+Enter to send)

work.queued: waiting for the item before it
work.queuedBody: This item of a work list waits for the item before it and starts by itself once that one is finished.

simple.title: What should we get done today?

subtitle.coding: Say what you want and the AI team builds it in your app folder. No technical knowledge needed.
subtitle.content: Give it your product material, say what to make, and the AI team writes the copy and content.
subtitle.finance: Drop in your sales or finance data and the AI team processes it and builds the report.
subtitle.admin: Drop in your documents and the AI team sorts them, fills in forms and tidies the archive.
subtitle.research: Say what to research and the AI team finds, analyses and writes it up, with sources.
subtitle.education: Give the topic and the audience; the AI team builds the material, exercises and quizzes.
subtitle.support: Drop in your policies and sample customer questions; the AI team writes replies, FAQs and SOPs.
subtitle.hr: Say which role you are hiring for; the AI team writes the post, screens CVs and prepares onboarding.
subtitle.legal: Drop in the documents and agreed points; the AI team drafts them. These are drafts, not legal advice: have a lawyer check them before use.
subtitle.ecommerce: Drop in your product data; the AI team writes listings, tidies the catalogue and plans promos.
subtitle.translation: Drop in the documents and name the target language; the AI team translates and edits.
subtitle.project: Describe the project or event; the AI team builds the timeline, the budget and the communication.
subtitle.custom: The team you built is ready. Write the job and the coordinator hands it to the best-fitting member.

setup.title: Connect an AI first (one time)
setup.body: OpenLeira needs one AI account to work. Pick the one you have; one is enough.

provider.claude: easiest if you have a Claude account
provider.codex: if you have a ChatGPT/OpenAI account
provider.opencode: if you have an OpenCode account or API key

setup.step1: Click "Connect" on the AI you have.
setup.step2: A login window opens. Follow the text on screen: usually open a link, log in in the browser, then paste a code if asked.
setup.step3: When done, close the window. If the status has not changed, click "Check again".
setup.preparingBody: The AI is connected. A model for each team member is picked for you automatically, nothing to set up. You can change it later in the full view.
setup.ready: AI connected: {{providers}}. The team is ready.
setup.autoFailed: The automatic model could not be set: {{message}}

materials.title: Add your material

body.content: Product photos/descriptions, catalogue, price list, examples of past content. The more you give, the better it fits.
body.finance: Excel/CSV files with sales data, receipts or last month's report. Original files are never changed.
body.admin: The documents to handle: scans, PDFs, blank forms, requirement lists.
body.research: Documents, links, notes or data you already have on the topic.
body.education: Syllabus, old books/modules, company SOPs or notes to turn into material.
body.support: Store policies (returns, shipping, warranty), sample customer chats/complaints, product list.
body.hr: Role descriptions, applicant CVs (PDF), company rules or past job posts.
body.legal: Past contracts, company templates, agreed points, details of the parties.
body.ecommerce: Product list (Excel/CSV), photos, cost and sale prices, stock, marketplace rules.
body.translation: Documents to translate, a glossary of fixed terms, past translations.
body.project: Project brief, vendor/price lists, meeting notes, attendee lists.
body.custom: Any files the team needs to work.

materials.optional: You can skip this if you have no material. You can also drag files here.
